answer: An agent economy can tax the exit instead of the door. Earnings leave only across one bridge to outside chains, and that bridge clusters destination wallets by their on-chain funding history. A farm can mine through a thousand heads, but it must sweep to one treasury in the end, so payouts converging on one cluster are released at a single agent's rate and the rest is escrowed for audits drawn by a public randomness beacon. Like an opal, a farm shows its true color only when turned over: look at where the money lands.
